ONE is designed to make materials not yet known to mankind. Materials that engineers dream about. Materials that give us lighter, stronger and more efficient products.

Freemelt offers a complete product portfolio supporting you from early material and process development through application development, into a seamless transition to serial production within industries such as medtech, orthopedic implants, energy, defense, and beyond.
The implant workhorse

Titanium alloy is a key material in orthopedic implants due to its strength, lightness, biocompatibility, and corrosion resistance. Freemelt’s E-PBF technology enhances titanium implant production by enabling complex geometries like solid cores with porous surfaces, and efficient stacking to boost productivity.

Tungsten’s heat resistance and density are vital for Fusion Energy, Defense, and medical X-ray equipment. Freemelt’s E-PBF technology overcomes the challenges of tungsten’s high melting point and brittleness, producing dense, crack-free parts with minimal oxygen uptake, opening new possibilities.

Freemelt has received an order from Alsymex, a subsidiary of the French technology group ALCEN and a strategic supplier to the ITER fusion energy project. The order represents an initial step in the qualification of advanced tungsten components for future ITER applications. The order value amounts to SEK 3,3 million, with final delivery scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

Tungsten is a critical material for future fusion reactors due to its ability to withstand extreme temperatures and demanding operating environments. Following ITER’s decision to transition from beryllium to tungsten in plasma-facing applications, a number of qualification activities are underway to evaluate advanced tungsten materials and components for future reactor systems.

“This project represents an important milestone in the ongoing qualification of tungsten for fusion energy applications. Being selected to contribute to one of the first ITER-related qualification programmes validates both our materials expertise and our capability to manufacture advanced tungsten components for demanding industrial applications,”

Freemelt builds Europe’s industrial platform for advanced metal components. Freemelt has been recognized as Innovation Pioneer at the 2026 F4E Supply Chain Awards by Fusion for Energy (F4E), the organization responsible for Europe’s contribution to ITER.

The award was presented on October 29, 2026 and recognizes outstanding contributions to Europe’s fusion supply chain. F4E works with more than 3,000 companies across 23 European countries in support of ITER and other fusion-related initiatives.

F4E recognized Freemelt for its additive manufacturing technology based on electron-beam powder bed fusion route for tungsten plasma-facing components. The route exceeded F4E’s requirements and led to an F4E contract for more than 30,000 tiles and monoblocks for JT-60SA.

The Rights Issue in Brief

The Company’s shareholders have preferential rights to subscribe for shares in the Rights Issue, whereby each existing share entitles the holder to one (1) subscription right, and 3 subscription rights entitle the holder to subscribe for 2 new shares.
The record date for participation in the Rights Issue is 24 November 2026. The last day of trading in the Company’s shares including the right to participate in the Rights Issue is 20 November 2026.
The subscription period in the Rights Issue will run from 26 November to 10 December 2026.
The Rights Issue is fully covered, up to 100 per cent, by subscription commitments, intentions to enter into subscription commitments and underwriting undertakings.

The Rights Issue is subject to approval by an extraordinary general meeting to be held on 20 November 2026. Notice of the extraordinary general meeting will be published through a separate press release.

The net proceeds from the Rights Issue will be used to scale Freemelt’s Manufacturing and Production Systems businesses, supporting capacity expansion, customer project execution, working capital, and the development of a more scalable recurring revenue base.
